_README: Shared staging-inference defaults. This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH:
infer_stage.py reads it when no override is passed on the command line, so
the launcher's Worm Survival run and the capture web UI's 'Analyze on
laptop' button start from identical numbers. The launcher also reads it to
seed the per-class sliders and to power their 'Reset to defaults' button.
class_conf: per-class confidence floor, applied to every raw tile detection
BEFORE the boxes are merged. '_default' covers any class not named here,
so a retrained model that adds a class still runs. Key order is the order
the launcher shows the sliders in - keep it in model-class order.
PROVENANCE OF THESE NUMBERS: chosen, not calibrated. They lift the classes
the model is known to be shakiest on (adult, and the L2/L3 boundary the
survival cutoff sits on) off the old uniform 0.25 and leave the rest near
it. Run dev/tools/stage_conf_report.py on a real plate set to replace them
with values read off the actual confidence distribution. Until then,
staging counts remain a QA readout, not data - see BACKLOG.md.

_comment: overlap only. tile_w/tile_h/imgsz are deliberately NOT settable here:
staging reads absolute worm size, so changing them silently degrades
accuracy. overlap moves where the seams fall without touching scale.
0.20 -> 56 tiles, whole-object guarantee 135x122 px
0.30 -> 63 tiles, whole-object guarantee 203x182 px
0.35 -> 72 tiles, whole-object guarantee 237x213 px (~29% slower than 0.20)
Targeted duplicate-box fix. A detection within margin_px of an INTERIOR
tile seam is flagged as a possible worm fragment, and dropped only if at
least cover_frac of its area sits inside a higher-scoring box of any
class. A fragment nothing covers is kept, so a worm is never lost.
Set cover_frac to null to disable the pass.
class_agnostic_iou: one extra NMS across ALL classes after the per-class
pass, for the case of ONE worm carrying TWO labels at nearly the same box
(the classic L3-here/L4-there pair). Per-class NMS cannot see that pair at
all - it only ever compares boxes of the same class.
At 0.70 two boxes must be almost the same rectangle to be merged, which
one object produces and two neighbouring worms realistically do not.
LOWER it (~0.55) if same-worm pairs still slip through; RAISE it if two
genuinely adjacent worms are being collapsed into one. null = off, which
is the pre-2026-07-27 behaviour.

_exclude_classes_README: Classes dropped from the run entirely, before any merge. Default is eggs:
a plate is almost never a question about worms AND eggs at the same time,
and egg boxes are pure clutter on a staging plate. Egg counts are wanted
for an egg-survival assay or a drop of bleached eggs — tick 'Count eggs'
in the launcher's Worm Survival card, or on the capture UI's Analyze
button, and that run keeps them.
Eggs are already excluded from the survival denominator (SURVIVAL_CONFIG
in survival.py), so this changes the egg column and the clutter, never the
An excluded class is NOT a class that scored zero. counts.txt prints
'not counted', the Excel drops the column, and run_info names the
exclusion — printing 0 would read as 'no eggs on this plate'.
Set to [] to count everything by default.

_README: Per-class plausible box size, as [min, max] of sqrt(width * height) in
full-frame pixels. Either bound may be null. A class absent from this
block is not size-gated at all.
WHY THIS EXISTS: staging is a size readout - the stages are ordered
egg < L1 < L2 < L3 < L4 < young adult < adult. A small round speck of
debris scoring 0.8 on 'adult' is not an uncertain adult, it is not a worm,
and no confidence threshold can fix that because the model is confident.
A size gate can: an adult-sized label on a debris-sized box is impossible
regardless of score.
EMPTY BY DEFAULT ON PURPOSE. The pixel size of a stage depends on the
magnification, so there is no honest default to ship - a guessed number
here deletes real worms. Measure it:
launcher\vision\.venv-vision\Scripts\python.exe ^
dev\tools\stage_conf_report.py --suggest "C:\path\to\images"
That writes stage_conf_suggested.json with a ready-to-paste block plus a
count of what each bound would have removed. Read the removal counts
before pasting.
Boxes flagged as seam-truncated are exempt from this gate - a worm clipped
by a tile edge is legitimately undersized and is handled by the seam pass.
